paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Jesus does not shrug at a heart that keeps its arms crossed. The cities where He did most of His miracles heard "Woe to you" because they did not repent (Matthew 11:20-21). Seeing the miracles was never the finish line. Turning toward Him was.

Now look at who gets the good news. Jesus praises the Father because He has hidden these things "from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children" (Matthew 11:25). I think that means knowing God is not a prize for the smartest person in the room. Jesus says no one knows the Father except the Son "and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him" (Matthew 11:27). So you don't climb up to God. He reveals Himself, and that is GOOD news for anybody who has ever felt a step behind.

And then comes the invitation. "Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28). Jesus calls Himself "gentle and humble in heart," and says "My yoke is easy and My burden is light" (Matthew 11:29-30). Baker, if you're tired today, you don't have to fix yourself first. Just come to Him.
